newsitem.title: USA: NGPL lifts "critical time" natgas order.
newsitem.headline: NGPL lifts "critical time" natgas order.

text.p: Natural Gas Pipeline (NGPL) said Friday it lifted the "critical time" order on its Texas-Illinois gas pipeline, effective Friday at 1200 CST.
"Effective Friday January 17, they lifted the critical time. It's for the gas day Friday, which starts at noon (1200 CST)," a company spokeswoman said.

The company also said the operational flow order (OFO) for the market delivery zone issued January 16 directed to limiting hourly takes is revised to 140 percent effective 0600 CST/1200 GMT on Saturday, January 18.

"During the hours of 0600 CST to 1200 CST each day, shippers and point operators are required to limit their takes on an aggregate basis at each delivery point in the market delivery zone to an hourly rate of no more than 140 percent of the hourly aggregate confirmed nominations plus no-notice rights at each such delivery point," the OFO said.
NGPL's system runs via two main lines from western Texas, terminating in Illinois.

Critical time or critical day orders are typically declared by pipeline operators during periods of extreme cold to ensure customers buying firm transmission receive their gas and to avoid operational problems on the system. Withdrawals from the system that exceed nominated volumes incur a penalty.
